docs.title: SDCF: A Bus With No Master
docs.text:
Self-Configuring Deterministic Control Fabric: microcontroller nodes on a shared RS-485 bus that give themselves collision-free time slots and cover for each other's failures, with no master node and no offline engineering.

Target: IEEE conference paper · Technical manuscript ~7,200 words

docs.title: The problem
docs.text: Factory machines are coordinated by fieldbuses such as EtherCAT, PROFINET IRT or TSN. They are deterministic, but they depend on a master node or a schedule engineered offline. If the master fails, or a node is added, someone has to intervene.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
SDCF puts low-cost microcontrollers (PIC18F57Q83) on a shared RS-485 multi-drop bus. Every node runs the same schedule function on a replicated table, so all nodes reach the same answer independently:

  • Masterless slot self-allocation. Nodes claim TDMA slots among themselves and converge to a collision-free schedule.
  • Join and admission. New nodes join with contention and binary exponential backoff; admission control keeps the schedule within its period.
  • Buddy fault takeover. When a node goes silent, a designated peer takes over its duties within a bounded number of frames.

The defensible gap: masterless, hard-deterministic slot self-allocation, with control-period-aware bandwidth assignment and bounded-latency peer fault takeover, on sub-$10 hardware over a wired multi-drop bus.

docs.title: Physical layer
docs.text: SDCF runs on RS-485, a wired multi-drop bus that is cheap, robust and already common in industrial equipment. Each node is a PIC18F57Q83: a deterministic core with no cache, so exact timing bounds can be derived from the datasheet and the compiled instruction listing.

docs.title: Time-division schedule
docs.text:
Time on the bus is divided into frames, and each frame into slots. Every node owns one or more slots and transmits only in its own slots, so frames never collide.

sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Node A
  participant B as Node B
  participant C as Node C
  Note over A,C: Frame n
  A->>A: slot 0: A transmits
  B->>B: slot 1: B transmits
  C->>C: slot 2: C transmits
  Note over A,C: Every node runs the same schedule function on the same table, so every node agrees on who owns which slot

docs.title: Protocol mechanisms
docs.text: Mechanism What it does Masterless slot self-allocation Nodes claim slots without a coordinator and converge to a collision-free schedule Anchor election Nodes agree on a timing anchor so frames stay aligned Join contention New nodes contend for entry using binary exponential backoff Admission control Bandwidth is assigned with each node's control period in mind; a join that would break the period is refused Buddy fault takeover Each node has a peer that takes over its role if it stops transmitting, within a bounded number of frames

docs.title: Timing method
docs.text: Hard timing bounds come from static worst-case execution time (WCET) analysis by instruction-cycle counting on the PIC18F57Q83, not from a laptop simulation. The simulator measures protocol-level quantities only: convergence frames, collision counts and takeover latency.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All results are protocol-level simulation results from the canonical Python simulator.

Measurement Result Convergence, 63 nodes Collision-free schedule within 88 frames, worst case Peer (buddy) takeover after a node fails 3 frames, against an analytical bound of 4 Experiment sweep 1,436 simulation runs with zero slot collisions and zero replica disagreements

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
• Convergence shows that a bus of 63 nodes reaches a deterministic schedule on its own, with no master and no configuration step.
  • Takeover shows that a failed node's duties are picked up inside a bounded time, which is what a control loop needs to stay safe.
  • No replica disagreements shows that every node, running the same function on the same table, always reached the same schedule.

docs.text: A reference firmware implementation is underway in MPLAB X, and the WCET constants for the timing analysis are being derived from the compiled listing. Hardware measurements will be added here as they are taken.
